claims.text: Tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys are candidate materials for fusion plasma-facing components.
Introducing stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitates governs high-temperature plastic strain and toughness in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces relieve local stress concentrations that can cause premature crack initiation.
Relieving stress concentrations delays premature crack initiation.
The combined dislocation-transmission and stress-relief effects produce more uniform plastic strain and improved elevated-temperature toughness.
A tailored alloy-design and heat-treatment protocol can generate stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitates.
An ideal nanoprecipitate interparticle spacing is required for favorable interaction with dislocations.
At 800 °C, the SCCP alloy retains high strength.
The proposed mechanism remains operative above 800 °C under both tensile and creep loading.
Relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, SCCP-treated material will have higher elevated-temperature ductility and plastic-strain capacity.
Relative to the baseline, SCCP-treated material will have improved elevated-temperature toughness.
SCCP-treated material will exhibit more efficient dislocation motion and fewer stress concentrators than material lacking coherent nanoprecipitates.
Incoherent precipitates do not facilitate dislocation movement in the manner proposed for coherent precipitates.
The mechanism is bounded to tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys in which precipitate coherence can be controlled.
The magnitude of improvement depends on precipitate size, spacing, and degree of coherence.
Other unisolated microstructural features may influence the measured mechanical outcome.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant increase in plastic strain and toughness relative to the control would falsify the hypothesis.
An absence of any coherent-precipitate-correlated difference in dislocation behavior would falsify the proposed mechanism.
